description: Python ecosystem groupings (pep621/uv/poetry). Most rules bundle peer-dep or hard-pinned stacks that must move together (boto3/botocore is the strictest); scientific-python is explicitly churn reduction rather than break prevention. Each rule states which it is. `sentry-sdk` DELIBERATELY HAS NO RULE (decided 2026-09-25, ahead of trip-tracker and youth-activity-scheduler adopting it). It is ONE PyPI package whose integrations are extras (`sentry-sdk[fastapi]`), so a group would have one member. Its extras declare only floors (`fastapi>=0.79.0`, `starlette>=0.19.1`, `celery>=3`) and it detects framework versions at runtime, so there is no coupling to `fastapi-stack` or `celery` to protect. If a rule is ever added, scope it `matchManagers: [pep621]`, because npm has an unrelated `sentry-sdk` package (the `vine`/`playwright` hazard). Name it `sentry-python`, never `sentry`: that is node.json's group name, and a shared groupName merges both ecosystems onto one branch (the `opentelemetry-python`/`opentelemetry-js` convention).

packageRules.description: boto3 + botocore + the transfer/async siblings. botocore is HARD-PINNED by boto3 to a narrow range (boto3 1.x.y requires botocore >=1.3x.y,<1.3x.y+1), so a split major is not a drift risk — it is an immediate unsatisfiable-resolution failure on whichever half lands first. The strongest coupling in this file. `aiobotocore` and `s3transfer` pin botocore the same way. NAMED `boto3`, NOT `aws-sdk` — do NOT rename it to match node.json's AWS group. A groupName is a branch name, so two rules sharing one name share one PR even across managers and preset files; since youth-activity-scheduler and claude-terminal-home-assistant extend BOTH :node and :python, a shared `aws-sdk` name would merge unrelated @aws-sdk/* and boto3 updates into a single cross-manager PR. The `matchManagers` scope below does NOT prevent this: it controls which deps MATCH, not which branch they land on.

PyTorch trio — torchvision and torchaudio are compiled against an exact torch version and are published per torch release; a split leaves a binary extension linked to a torch ABI that is no longer installed, which surfaces as an import-time symbol error rather than a resolver failure.

LangChain — `langchain`, `langchain-core`, and the `langchain-*` provider packages all pin langchain-core and move on one release cadence; the core interfaces change across minors, so even a non-major skew can break provider imports.

OpenTelemetry Python — api/sdk/exporters/instrumentation share a registered global provider and are published as one release set; mixing versions silently drops spans. Mirrors the `/^@opentelemetry//` rule in node.json in intent, but the group name is deliberately DIFFERENT from it (`opentelemetry-js` there) — see the `boto3` rule above for why a shared name would merge the two ecosystems onto one branch.

Celery + its transport/execution stack — kombu, billiard, and vine are cut per celery release and pinned narrowly by it. NOTE the `matchManagers: [pep621]` scope is load-bearing here beyond this file's convention: `vine` is ALSO a real npm package name, and a consumer extending both :node and :python would otherwise have an unrelated JS package pulled into the Celery group — the same cross-ecosystem accident the playwright rule in node.json guards against with matchDatasources.

PRE-SEEDED. Django + DRF + the django-* plugin ecosystem: plugins declare their supported Django major and are re-cut per Django LTS, so a core major without its plugins fails at app-registry load. The `/^django-/` regex covers third-party plugins, which is acceptable here (unlike the tailwind-merge case in node.json) because the django-* prefix is a community convention specifically for Django-version-coupled packages.
PRE-SEEDED. Hugging Face stack — transformers pins tokenizers to a narrow range and both track huggingface-hub's API; datasets and accelerate follow the same cadence.

PRE-SEEDED. numpy + scipy + pandas. CHURN REDUCTION, NOT BREAK PREVENTION — stated plainly so the justification is not misread: these are independent projects and a split major usually resolves fine. They are grouped only because scipy and pandas compile against numpy's C ABI, so a numpy major is the event that drags the other two, and reviewing them on three branches hides that. Do NOT extend this rule to the wider scientific stack on the same reasoning.

Track `requires-python` through the NATIVE pep621 manager ONLY when it is an exact `==X.Y.Z` pin; every other shape is disabled here. Floor ranges (`>=3.10`), compatible ranges (`~=3.14`), wildcards (`==3.14.*`), two-part pins (`==3.14`), arbitrary equality (`===3.14.7`) and compound specifiers (`==3.14.7,<4`) are min-version METADATA, not a runtime pin, and must never move: left enabled, the fleet's top-level `rangeStrategy: pin` turns `>=3.14` into a `pin` update to `==3.14.N`. The exact triple IS a runtime pin, and the next rule groups it with the `python` base image. WHY NATIVE (this replaced a regex customManager, 2026-10): uv.lock carries its OWN `requires-python`, so the pyproject bump alone fails every uv job with `The current Python version (<new>) is not compatible with the locked Python requirement: ==<old>`. The pep621 manager runs the uv artifact step: `uv lock --upgrade-package python`, with the CPython toolchain taken from the UPDATED `requires-python`. Renovate therefore commits the regenerated uv.lock itself, a one-line `requires-python` change with no package movement. A regex customManager only substitutes text and never runs that step, so every `python runtime` PR used to open red and need a hand-pushed `uv lock` commit (owine/trip-tracker #282). That push was also a trap: once a human commits to a Renovate branch, Renovate treats it as edited and stops updating it, which strands any half of the group that has not landed yet. MATCHING: `!/…/` is a NEGATED regex (Renovate's getRegexPredicate inverts the result), so this one rule disables everything except the triple. `[ \t]*` after `==` keeps the old regex manager's whitespace tolerance. pep440 rewrites `==3.14.7` to `==3.14.8` under both `pin` and `replace` with no widening, and normalises `== 3.14.7` to `==3.14.8`. Matched by depType, not depName: the extractor sets only `packageName: python` and depName is backfilled from it, so a depName match cannot tell the `requires-python` line apart from a dependency that happens to be named `python`. MEND-HOSTED: the artifact step installs that exact CPython through containerbase. The `python-version` datasource only offers versions that already have a `containerbase/python-prebuild` release, so whatever Renovate proposes is installable. If the install or `uv lock` still fails, the PR still opens with the pyproject bump and an UNCHANGED uv.lock. It is not silent: Renovate posts an `Artifact update problem` comment with uv's stderr and fails the `renovate/artifacts` status, and the retry checkbox re-runs the artifact step. `postUpgradeTasks` stays unused because Mend-hosted does not allow it.

Group the exact-pinned `requires-python` (pep621 manager, depType `requires-python`, packageName `python`; see the rule above) into the same PR as the `python` Docker base image (dockerfile manager, depName `python`), so an exact CPython pin and its base image never bump separately and drift apart. Split, NEITHER half can go green alone: the base-image-only PR fails `No interpreter found for Python <old>` (pyproject still pins the old triple), and the pyproject-only PR fails the Docker build the same way in reverse, because the old base image cannot satisfy the new pin — owine/trip-tracker #180/#182. CONFLICT RESOLUTION: if the system Python ever fails to satisfy the exact pin, uv silently falls back to a uv-managed standalone interpreter (unreachable by a non-root runtime user). Consumers MUST set `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never` so that mismatch fails the build loudly instead. `internalChecksFilter: none` IS WHAT KEEPS THE TWO HALVES ON ONE BRANCH. Under the default `strict`, Renovate drops every pending upgrade from a branch as long as one other upgrade on it is NOT pending (`generateBranchConfig`: `Branch is not pending, removing pending upgrades`), and a pending dep falls back to its newest already-soaked release. The halves are aged by different datasources (see the next rule), so `strict` split this group whenever their clocks disagreed: owine/trip-tracker #282 (3.14.8) and #316 (3.15.0) opened with only `requires-python` and failed docker-build with `No interpreter found for Python 3.15.0`. A half dropped this way gets no dashboard checkbox, because the branch already exists through the other half. `strict` could also put DIFFERENT versions in one branch: pyproject falling back to a soaked 3.14.9 while the image took 3.15.0. Under `none` every half always targets the newest release, so the halves always agree and nothing is dropped. THE SOAK IS NOT REMOVED; IT MOVES FROM BRANCH CREATION TO MERGE. The branch opens with both halves, and Renovate's `renovate/stability-days` status stays pending until every upgrade on it has met its own `minimumReleaseAge`. That blocks automerge: `internalChecksAsSuccess` is unset fleet-wide, so a pending `renovate/` check keeps the branch yellow. A major is manual-merge anyway and shows that check pending for the full 7 days. DELIBERATELY NOT `prCreation: not-pending` to get creation-gating back: GitHub's branch status discards successful `renovate/*` checks and reports `pending` when nothing else has reported, so in a consumer whose CI runs only on `pull_request` the PR would never open. RESIDUAL GAP, SELF-HEALING: if one registry lists a release before the other (python-version waits for a containerbase/python-prebuild release, Docker Hub for the official-images build), a run inside that gap opens the branch with one half. It is red at docker-build and cannot automerge, and the missing half joins on the next run once its registry has it (`updateNotScheduled` defaults to true), usually within hours. Do NOT push a fix to the branch: a human commit makes Renovate treat the branch as edited and stop updating it, which strands the half that has not landed. Both image spellings are listed because `FROM docker.io/library/python:X` yields the fully-qualified depName rather than the bare `python`, mirroring docker.json's runtime-major label rule. Plain strings are glob-matched with `.`/`/` literal, so these match exactly and leave `python-slim`/`my.registry/python` alone. This holds regardless of `extends` order ONLY because docker.json's `dockerfile bases` rule negates these same two names. That rule matches `matchManagers: [dockerfile]`, so with :python extended before :docker it would otherwise win the groupName and pull the base image back out. Keep this list and that negation in sync. MAJORS: intentionally no `matchUpdateTypes` — the group applies to majors too, because a runtime major has exactly the same drift hazard as a patch and the two deps always bump to the same version. This does not weaken the fleet's major policy: default.json's `separateMajorMinor`/`separateMultipleMajor` still isolate the major onto its own branch, and its major rule still applies the 7-day soak (to the `python-version` half; the image exemption below exempts the image), `automerge: false`, and the `major-update`/`needs-review` labels. A CPython MINOR gets the same manual review from the next rule, because for Python that is the release that actually breaks things. Grouping only decides which deps share that branch, not how it is reviewed. MEMBERS BEYOND THE PIN AND THE IMAGE: pyenv's `.python-version` (depName `python`, datasource docker); the `uv python install` workflow customManager below (depName `python`, datasource `python-version`); and `actions/python-versions`, the packageName Renovate's github-actions manager gives `actions/setup-python`'s `python-version:` input (and setup-miniconda's). That last one is PRE-SEEDED: no fleet repo passes setup-python a version (2026-10-19). Without it, the input lands on automerge.json's ci bundle and bumps on its own, because the bare `python` entry cannot reach a dep whose packageName is `actions/python-versions`. COMMIT TYPE `deps:` IS LOAD-BEARING once workflow lines are members. default.json types every github-actions dep and every `.github/workflows/**` dep `ci:`. A branch takes the highest-priority type among its upgrades, and `deps` is unranked, so ONE CI line would retype a CPython bump of the shipped image `ci:`, which release-please hides (the unifi-protect-mcp #284 mechanism). Typing the whole group `deps:` keeps a runtime bump releasing. THE COST: a branch made ONLY of workflow lines is `deps:` too and cuts a patch release with no shipped change. That only happens on a one-time catch-up (trip-tracker's stale `3.14` lines after #316), because a two-part CI line moves only on an X.Y release, which also moves the pin and the image. It is the less harmful of the two errors. `vulnerabilityAlerts` still retypes a security fix `fix:`, since it is applied as `force`. test/commit-types.mjs asserts the group carries one type.

A CPython MINOR (`3.14.x` -> `3.15.0`) is reviewed like a major: `automerge: false`, a 7-day soak, and the `breaking`/`needs-review` labels docker.json's runtime-major rule adds. WHY: for CPython the X.Y release IS the breaking-change event. It removes the deprecations the previous release scheduled, changes the ABI tag (`cp314` -> `cp315`), and every C-extension dependency needs a new wheel built for it. A true major (3 -> 4) is not on any roadmap, so the fleet's major rule (default.json) and docker.json's runtime-major labels never fire for Python. Before this rule a CPython minor was an ordinary non-major: automerge.json's bundle rule gave it `automerge: true` and this group only renamed its branch. owine/trip-tracker #316 (3.14.8 -> 3.15.0) was automerged by Renovate at 2026-10-19T14:42Z, 3 minutes after its Dockerfile half joined, with no human review. PATCHES are unaffected and keep automerging: an X.Y.Z bump is a bugfix/security release on a fixed ABI. THE 7-DAY SOAK mirrors the major rule because this is the fleet's major-equivalent event for Python, so it gets the same review surface. The soak is less about the interpreter than about wheels: a fresh `cp3XX` ABI needs time for compiled dependencies (pydantic-core, asyncpg, uvloop, ...) to publish wheels for it. It applies to the `python-version` half only. The image exemption rule below comes AFTER this one and puts the image back to `0 days` (see it for why). Under the group's `internalChecksFilter: none` the PR still opens immediately; the soak shows as a pending `renovate/stability-days` check, which is a signal on a manual-merge PR rather than a gate. ONE NON-AUTOMERGE HALF IS ENOUGH: `generateBranchConfig` sets branch automerge to `every(upgrade.automerge)` and unions `addLabels`, so the whole `python runtime` branch goes manual even if a later rule ever re-enabled automerge on one half. NOT SPLIT ONTO ITS OWN BRANCH: `separateMinorPatch` stays off fleet-wide, so a pending minor and patch already resolve to one update (the newest), and splitting the group by update type would put the same CPython version on two branches. PRECEDENCE: :python is extended after :automerge in every consumer, so this beats the bundle's `automerge: true`. No preset extended later (docker, node, alpine, home-assistant, mcp) sets automerge or `minimumReleaseAge` for these names. The only override is `vulnerabilityAlerts`, which is applied as `force` and still automerges a security fix, as it does for majors. MATCHING: the group rule's three names exactly. `python` catches the pep621 pin, pyenv `.python-version`, the Dockerfile image and the `uv python install` workflow lines; `docker.io/library/python` catches the qualified image spelling; `actions/python-versions` catches the setup-python input. The two image spellings are shared with the exemption below and docker.json's `dockerfile bases` negation; keep all four lists in sync. test/python-runtime.mjs runs every half through each consumer's real extends order.

Exempt the `python` Docker IMAGE from `minimumReleaseAge`. The `python-version` half of `python runtime` carries the soak. WHY: the docker datasource dates a tag by Docker Hub's `tag_last_pushed`, which is the LATEST push, not the first. Official images are re-pushed under the same tag every time the Debian base is rebuilt, and each re-push restarts the clock. `3.14.8-slim` was first pushed 2026-10-04 but Renovate later dated it 2026-10-09, and `3.15.0-slim` was dated 2026-10-17T14:08Z, eight days after CPython 3.15.0 (2026-10-09). In a busy week the image never reaches 3 days, so its age measures Debian churn rather than how long the release has been out. The image only repackages a CPython release whose own soak runs on the `python-version` datasource (CPython's release date). Both halves share one branch, so the group's `renovate/stability-days` check still stays pending until that release is 3 days old (7 for a major). SAFE ONLY TOGETHER WITH the group's `internalChecksFilter: none` (the group rule above). Under the default `strict`, an exempt image is never pending while a fresh `requires-python` is. Renovate then drops the pyproject half and opens a base-image-only PR, #316 in reverse, and that PR stays red until the CPython release has soaked. test/python-runtime.mjs proves both directions against Renovate's real filterInternalChecks/generateBranchConfig. SCOPE: `matchManagers: [dockerfile]` + `matchDatasources: [docker]` plus the two exact image spellings, mirrored from the group rule and the CPython-minor rule above and from docker.json's `dockerfile bases` negation (keep the image spellings in sync across all four). `matchManagers` IS LOAD-BEARING. Renovate's pyenv manager extracts `.python-version` as depName `python` with datasource `docker`: it looks the version up as a Docker Hub `library/python` tag. Without the manager scope this exemption therefore covered `.python-version` too, and in a `.python-version` + Dockerfile repo NO half carried the soak. Verified 2026-10-19 on owine/youth-activity-scheduler, whose `requires-python` is a disabled floor: a dry run resolved the 3.15.0 branch to `minimumReleaseAge: null` on both halves. Scoped, `.python-version` keeps the fleet soak, measured by Docker Hub's `tag_last_pushed` for the bare `X.Y.Z` tag. That clock has the re-push problem described above, but a re-push only ever makes a release look YOUNGER, never older. So the soak can run long (a patch automerge waits until the tag has gone three days without a re-push) but never short. Moving `.python-version` onto the `python-version` datasource would mean disabling the pyenv manager fleet-wide for a regex replacement, which is not worth it for one consumer whose minors are manual anyway. A `python` image used as a job `container:` or in docker-compose keeps the soak too; only the Dockerfile `FROM` is exempt. The `requires-python` half (datasource `python-version`), `python-slim`, `my.registry/python` and every other image keep the fleet soak. PRECEDENCE: this overrides default.json's 3-day baseline, its 7-day major rule AND the 7-day CPython-minor rule directly above (which is why it must stay after that rule), for the image only, because :python is always extended after the base preset. No preset extended later sets `minimumReleaseAge` for docker deps (alpine.json's `0 days` is apk-only). `0 days` rather than `null`: Renovate treats the two identically since 42.19.5, and `0 days` is the spelling default.json and alpine.json already use. Digest refreshes of the image are exempt too, which is intended, because a re-push IS a new digest and has the same re-dating problem.

`uv python install X.Y` in a workflow (the customManager below) keeps its precision: `3.14` -> `3.15`, and a triple stays a triple. The manager sets `npm` versioning, which reads a bare `3.14` as the x-range `3.14.x`, so a patch release still satisfies it (no update, no PR) and an X.Y release is rewritten at the same precision. `pep440`, `loose` and `semver-coerced` all read `3.14` as the exact version `3.14.0` and rewrite it to `3.15.0`, then churn on every patch. Renovate's own `actions/setup-python` extraction uses `npm` versioning for the same reason. `rangeStrategy: replace` IS LOAD-BEARING: default.json's top-level `rangeStrategy: pin` would turn the `3.14` range into a `pin` update to `3.14.8` on the first run (the same trap alpine.json documents for apk). `replace` changes nothing for a triple, which npm treats as an exact version and rewrites to the next triple. Matched by the manager's own `depTypeTemplate`, so no other workflow dep and no other `python` dep picks this up.

customManagers.description: Track `uv python install <X.Y | X.Y.Z>` in GitHub Actions workflows, datasource `python-version`, depName `python`, so the CI interpreter joins the `python runtime` group and bumps in the same PR as `requires-python`/`.python-version`/the base image. WHY: nothing tracked these lines. owine/trip-tracker moved to 3.15.0 (#316) and its four `uv python install 3.14` lines went stale unnoticed: every CI job downloaded CPython 3.14.8 (35 MB, unused), then `uv sync` downloaded 3.15.0 for the pinned `requires-python`. The drift costs time and bandwidth rather than a red build, because uv re-provisions whatever the project pins, but a step that runs `python` directly (not via `uv run`) tests the stale interpreter. CONSIDERED ALTERNATIVE: tell consumers to not pass a version at all (`uv sync` provisions from an exact `requires-python`, and a bare `uv python install` reads `.python-version`). That is the better workflow, and the README checklist recommends it, but a preset cannot enforce it, so this manager catches whoever does pass one. MATCHING: one version only, as the whole argument. A list (`install 3.13 3.14`, a test matrix) is left alone, because bumping its first entry would collapse two lanes into one. Free-threaded (`3.14t`), pre-release (`3.15.0rc1`), implementation-prefixed (`cpython@3.14`, `pypy@3.10`), `${{ matrix.* }}` and specifier (`>=3.12`) requests do not match. Leading value-less flags (`--default`, `-q`) and trailing flags are allowed. The terminator class (end of line, `;`, `&&`, `||`, `#`, `)`, `\`) is consumed rather than looked ahead to, because RE2 has no lookahead; auto-replace is literal splicing, so only the value changes. `[ \t]`, never `\s`, for the same cross-line hazard as default.json's workflow managers, and no inline `(?m)` flag (it breaks under the native-RegExp fallback). managerFilePatterns is default.json's workflow pattern exactly. PRECEDENCE: default.json types `.github/workflows/**` as `ci:` and automerge.json groups it as `all non-major ci dependencies`. Both are extended before :python, so the `python runtime` group rule above wins the groupName and resets the type to `deps:` (see it). `python-version` is the same datasource as the pep621 half, so this dep carries the soak (3 days, 7 for a minor). NOT COVERED: `astral-sh/setup-uv`'s `python-version:` input. Renovate does not extract it, no fleet repo uses it, and it would need a with-block-scoped regex. `actions/setup-python`'s `python-version:` IS extracted natively (packageName `actions/python-versions`) and is pre-seeded into the group above. test/custom-managers.mjs gates this regex against fixtures.
